pages.quiz:
INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES — TERMLY EXAM #6 (TERM 3)
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
TIME ALLOWED: 60 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which is a constructive leisure activity? (1 mark)
   A. Wasting money
   B. Reading a book
   C. Fighting
   D. Harming others

2. Which feeling does Ouch! show? (1 mark)
   A. Joy
   B. Disgust
   C. Pain
   D. Sleepiness

3. How should you read an interjection aloud? (1 mark)
   A. Very quietly always
   B. In a flat voice
   C. Without pausing
   D. With the feeling it shows

4. In the sentence Oops, it is torn, what is the interjection? (1 mark)
   A. Oops
   B. torn
   C. is
   D. it

5. How long should each line in a dialogue usually be? (1 mark)
   A. Short, like real speech
   B. Very long speeches
   C. One page
   D. None

6. Why do writers use interjections in dialogues? (1 mark)
   A. To make it longer
   B. To show feelings and make speech natural
   C. To hide the story
   D. To fill the page

7. Which word in a small silver radio is the noun? (1 mark)
   A. small
   B. silver
   C. radio
   D. a

8. Which sentence uses an adjective? (1 mark)
   A. The heavy computer is on the table.
   B. Computers work.
   C. On the table.
   D. The computer is on.

9. What is a headline? (1 mark)
   A. A price
   B. A short eye-catching title
   C. A picture
   D. The last word

10. What can you use to make a poster advert? (1 mark)
   A. Only a number
   B. A blank page
   C. Only a full stop
   D. A headline, picture, adjectives, price and place

11. What does a good form have? (1 mark)
   A. No spaces
   B. Clear title, instructions and enough space
   C. Tiny words only
   D. No title

12. What should you do after filling a form? (1 mark)
   A. Give it to anyone
   B. Throw it away
   C. Ignore it
   D. Check it and sign and date it

13. What is a talking object used for? (1 mark)
   A. To show who may speak
   B. To play with
   C. To hide
   D. To throw

14. Which is a good quality of a leader? (1 mark)
   A. Rudeness
   B. Laziness
   C. Cruelty
   D. Honesty

15. What is repetition in a poem? (1 mark)
   A. Adding a picture
   B. Deleting lines
   C. Repeating words or lines for effect
   D. Changing the title

16. Why do we read poems? (1 mark)
   A. To enjoy language and learn lessons
   B. To hide feelings
   C. To stop reading
   D. To waste time

17. What is a choral poem? (1 mark)
   A. A map
   B. A silent poem
   C. A poem performed by a group together
   D. A written test

18. What should you use in your answers to poem questions? (1 mark)
   A. Your favourite song
   B. Nothing
   C. Words from the poem
   D. A dictionary only

19. Which is a poor instruction? (1 mark)
   A. Do the thing with the papers
   B. Collect the exercise books and place them on the table
   C. Wet your hands
   D. Rinse the soap

20. What should you add when a task is dangerous? (1 mark)
   A. A colour
   B. A song
   C. A warning
   D. A joke

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
21. State three rules for a debate. (3 marks)

22. Explain why you should ask an elder or teacher about writing interjections in your mother tongue, and describe how to collect them. (5 marks)

23. Name two components of a poem. (2 marks)

24. Make an instruction chart of five steps for keeping the class clean. Include a title and start each step with a verb. (5 marks)

25. State three steps for writing a dialogue. (3 marks)

26. Match each interjection with its feeling: (a) Hurray (b) Yuck. (2 marks)

27. Name two parts of an advert. (2 marks)

28. Write the four parts of a telephone conversation and give a short example of one. (4 marks)

29. Describe how to read a passage with interjections aloud. (4 marks)
pages.answers:
INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES — TERMLY EXAM #6 (TERM 3) · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. B — Reading a book
   Constructive activities build people up.

2. C — Pain
   People say ouch when hurt.

3. D — With the feeling it shows
   Intonation shows feeling.

4. A — Oops
   Oops shows a small mistake.

5. A — Short, like real speech
   Real conversations use short turns.

6. B — To show feelings and make speech natural
   Interjections show emotions.

7. C — radio
   Radio names the thing.

8. A — The heavy computer is on the table.
   Heavy describes the computer.

9. B — A short eye-catching title
   A headline is the title of an advert or news item.

10. D — A headline, picture, adjectives, price and place
   Adverts have these parts.

11. B — Clear title, instructions and enough space
   Clarity makes forms easy to fill.

12. D — Check it and sign and date it
   Checking prevents mistakes.

13. A — To show who may speak
   Only the holder speaks.

14. D — Honesty
   Good leaders are honest and fair.

15. C — Repeating words or lines for effect
   Repetition emphasises an idea.

16. A — To enjoy language and learn lessons
   Poems entertain and teach.

17. C — A poem performed by a group together
   Chorus means together.

18. C — Words from the poem
   Answers should come from the poem.

19. A — Do the thing with the papers
   It is vague.

20. C — A warning
   Warnings keep people safe.

SECTION B
----
21. (3 marks)
   Answer: Listen without interrupting, speak politely, give reasons, accept the result graciously, take turns.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each rule.

22. (5 marks)
   Answer: Ask because spelling and meanings must be correct and not invented. Listen to speakers, write each interjection with its feeling on a flashcard, check spelling with the teacher and sort by feeling.
   Working / marking points: Two marks for the reason and three marks for collecting steps.

23. (2 marks)
   Answer: Title, lines, stanzas, rhyme, rhythm, message (any two).
   Working / marking points: One mark each.

24. (5 marks)
   Answer: Title: How to keep our class clean. 1. Sweep the floor. 2. Wipe the desks. 3. Put waste in the bin. 4. Wash your hands. 5. Close the windows.
   Working / marking points: One mark for the title, one mark for each of four steps that begin with verbs and are in order.

25. (3 marks)
   Answer: Choose theme, choose characters, decide setting, write each speaker on a new line, use interjections, read aloud.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each step.

26. (2 marks)
   Answer: (a) joy (b) disgust
   Working / marking points: One mark for each.

27. (2 marks)
   Answer: Headline, picture, description, price, contact details (any two).
   Working / marking points: One mark for each.

28. (4 marks)
   Answer: Greet; say who you are and why you called; talk and listen; say goodbye. Example: Good afternoon, this is Neema speaking.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each part and one mark for an example, with 4 marks maximum.

29. (4 marks)
   Answer: Read silently first, find the interjections, decide the feeling of each, read each with the right voice, and keep a steady pace.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each of four points.
